clue.text: Carol leaves Reading for the country

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so one word is taken out of the other

parts.note: reading a text closely is perusing it
to carol is to sing

explanation.surface: A singer of carols walks out of the English town of Reading and heads abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading looks like the Berkshire town but is the verb. 'leaves' takes SING out of PERUSING.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a South American nation, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: East German in the saddle, rider on the near side

parts.note: a pillion is a seat or saddle behind the rider

clue.text: Composer to get into a tangle?

explanation.surface: A musician who keeps getting himself knotted up.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Ravel wrote Bolero; as a verb the word means to tangle threads.

clue.text: Colleagues in a ship with ill-fated explorer going round islands

CI stands for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Fellow workers travelling on a vessel with a doomed polar explorer as it sails round some islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Lawrence Oates walked out to his death on Scott's 1912 South Pole expedition.
explanation.definitionFit: Associates are partners or companions at work, a plain synonym for colleagues.

clue.text: Drunk's sounding egotistical ——'crabby 'type?

indicators.note: a drunk's sounding means the word as slurred aloud by someone who has had too much

parts.note: egotistical means self-centred

explanation.surface: A drunkard mumbles that someone is a self-centred, grumpy type.
explanation.walkthrough: A drunk slurs the S of SELFISH into SH. 'crabby type' looks like bad temper but means a creature like a crab.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs are crustaceans, an example of a marine creature with a hard exterior.

clue.text: One has something getting some children worried, upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read bottom to top
some means only part of these words is used

explanation.surface: A person with possessions is worrying a few children and upsetting them.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessor is someone who has property, so this person has something.

clue.text: Occupy hospital, soon being taken outside

indicators.note: the phrase for soon goes round the other letter

parts.note: in a bit means soon

explanation.surface: Patients taking over a hospital who will soon be taken outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhabit a place is to live in or occupy it.

clue.text: Significant error is made — violent intimidation being covered up

indicators.note: covered up means concealed within the surrounding words

explanation.definitionFit: Terrorism is the use of violence to frighten people for political ends.

clue.text: Body of prophet heaven-bound

parts.note: Amos is an Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: A prophet's corpse rising to heaven.

clue.text: Man on board when many are in bunks reportedly?

parts.note: most people are in bed at night

explanation.definitionFit: The knight is a chess piece, and chessmen are pieces on a board.

clue.text: Number observed, possibly meeting inside

clue.text: Bad English girl breaking the rules

gal is an informal word for a girl

clue.text: Strip tease — good in Paris

clue.text: Flavoured alcohol that journalist's found in rooms

clue.text: Shocked, given rude adjective in Latin form

clue.text: Chopped herb is divine
